title: AI trading Help needed.
author: gto40069
selftext: Im pretty novice at this however i downloaded Robinhood trading years ago and bought a few stocks, which all did go up, but i didnt sell and shortly after they tanked and a few went bankrupt. The few stocks and crypto that i had yet were so far upside down that there’s no hope for them. So i didnt log into Robinhood for probably a year at least. My work schedule does not make it easy to keep an eye on the market and to buy and sell when the time is right. I saw all the ads for the apps with AI trading built in and i did consider, but shortly after i saw Robinhood now had it where you could link up an AI agent. I did this and gave it a try. I have had a few stocks that i did get a slight profit on, but more losses than wins. I have tried both Claude and ChatGPT but im pretty novice using AI as well. Unless having it help come up with home finishing ideas count. Can anyone point me in a more solid direction on how to go about this? I am currently using ChatGPT and just have it run scans every hour, but im consistently getting no trades recommended or recommended sell because a stock is down, (Which i have done) and then 2 weeks later it is up higher than previously.  I could use some pointers, directions, help, or whatever else i may be missing.

comments.author: IndependentBid6893
comments.body:
I created [https://www.clawstreet.io/](https://www.clawstreet.io/) for this reason, to test and tune AI models before wasting cash on bad trades. It simulates slippage and fees so can help show faults with your agent. IF you agent fails on Clawstreet, you can just create a new version or replace it.  
  
Not trying to sell you on anything theres a free plan which lets you do most of what you need to test and learn. Hopefully if helps. I started it because I wanted to test and see agents run for months before deploying to real markets.

Some of this might be helpful to read as well: [https://www.clawstreet.io/blog/agentic-trading-guide](https://www.clawstreet.io/blog/agentic-trading-guide)

Good luck!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the agent isn't really the problem, nobody gave it a tested rule, so it guesses. with your hours I'd keep most of it in a broad index fund and leave any agent on fake money for a few months. I built a tool for that paper step, Quantradin. quantradin.com

comments.author: steady-action
comments.body: I strongly don’t recommend you to start trading with agent right away. So many people do not understand agentic trading does not make you win. What makes you win is a good strategy. Until you have a good strategy you will just lose money automatically. I would get started by using a tool like Alphaground to set up and test out AI trading agents with strategies.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I can't tell you what to buy, but a few things would give you more to work with. An hourly scan with no written rules produces noisy advice, so write down in plain terms what you want (how much per trade, a maximum loss per position, when you'd sell and why), and let the AI check trades against those rules and not invent them. Keep your size small and track every trade in a simple log with the reason and the result, so after a month you can see whether anything beats just holding an index fund. Selling because a stock is down is often the reverse of a plan, and earnings dates and macro releases cause many of those sharp moves. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for knowing when they're due.
